stem:
Calvin draws two congruent figures. He shades an equal area of each figure.
Which figures could be Calvin’s?

options.label: A
options.text: Two circles each divided into four equal parts, one part shaded in each, with the larger circle's shaded part half the size but same fraction as smaller circle's shaded part.

options.label: B
options.text: Two hexagonal figures split into six triangles each, one small triangle shaded in each, matching in shaded fraction despite different shape presentation.

options.label: C
options.text: Two squares each divided into four parts; one is a square with one quarter shaded and the other a square divided by diagonals with one triangular quarter shaded.

options.label: D
options.text: Two large triangles each subdivided into four smaller triangles; shaded regions include three of the four in first and one of the four in second.

visual_elements: Four pairs of geometric figures labeled A, B, C, and D, with shaded areas indicating fractions of the figures's areas.
difficulty_rationale: Requires understanding of congruency and fractional areas, and comparing shapes and shaded regions computationally.
